items.source: Item 1. David Winn, 'A Dual to Ordinary Matter Yielding Composite Flavored Scalar Dark Matter', Lepton-Photon 2025, Indico 1493037, contribution 6549576 (#177): the abstract, 27 slides ('Monopolium talk 2025_12.pdf') and a 5-page summary (10 Nov 2025).
items.quotes_found: All 32. I downloaded the page, the export JSON and both PDFs myself and found each quotation by code in my own text, on the slide or page given. Match levels: 11 exact; 12 after whitespace normalization; 2 only after mapping the Symbol-font code points U+F061→α and U+F062→β (both code points are in the export JSON and the page HTML); 7 only after stripping spaces or line-break hyphens, because pypdf drops spaces around Greek letters and subscripts.
items.relation_corrections:
No label is stronger than its evidence. C4 shared-photon 'partial' holds: Winn has a magnetic partner for each electrically charged particle under our own photon, hidden by the binding route of §11.4; the p-polarization is missing, and v-winn says so.
- C7 'not relevant' stands, but its reason ('the dark-dark forces are short-range') is contradicted by Winn's own words: 'long-range chromomagnetic di-gluino exchange provides additional binding among neutral composites.' (summary p. 3). The ranges he implies are microscopic: 85.8 fm for the 2.3 MeV squark, about 2 nm for slide 9's 'sub-0.1 KeV' (computed). Nothing is gated by relative velocity.
- C5 'not relevant' is defensible. 'Related (theme only)' would also fit (my judgment): dark energy comes from the Dual's photino, 'generating a Fermi pressure at universe scale wavelengths -Dark Energy-' (summary p. 5), with no collapse.
- C1 monopole form: the reason that 't Hooft–Polyakov 'enters only as motivation and to set a pole size' leaves out that it also sets the charge quantum: 't’Hooft-Polyakov Dirac quantization g=2e/α' (summary p. 1).

items.source: Item 2. David R. Winn, 'SUSY Via Magnetic Monopoles and Chirality', arXiv:1206.4590 [physics.gen-ph], 10 pp., INSPIRE recid 1118961.
items.quotes_found: All 12, found by code in my pypdf text of PDF v1, each on the page given (all match after whitespace normalization).
items.relation_corrections:
Add a C6 label: related. The paper proposes Bose condensates of right-handed sneutrinos as dark matter:
- 'may form Bose condensates – hence Dark Matter - in the cosmos.' (p. 3; the sneutrino glyph extracts as '!')
- 'These handed complex scalars may form Bose condensates as a part of Dark Matter.' (p. 5)
- 'condensates also contribute to Dark Matter, and may provide the bulk of it' (p. 7)

A condensate is macroscopic occupation of the lowest momentum mode, the wave-dark-matter case that App. A item 3 discusses. Winn never says 'momentum space' or 'clumping', and the remark is a passing speculation, so the label is related, not partial.

C5 'not relevant' is defensible. 'Related (theme only)' would fit (my judgment): §20 gives photinos as dark energy, 'forms a fully relativistic Fermi Gas with a negative pressure similar to that indicated by observational Dark Energy' (p. 4).

The other labels hold.
items.note:
Confirmed from my own downloads of the abstract page, the API record and the PDF.
- v1 was submitted Mon, 18 Jun 2012 18:29:31 UTC and is the only version.
- PDF CreationDate 2012-06-18 18:09:51 UTC, Word title 'Magneto_SUSY14'. INSPIRE shows 0 citations. 5187 full days before 2026-09-01 (computed).

The precursor link is stronger than v-winn shows:
- By code, 40.6% of the 2012 paper's distinct 8-word sequences recur in the 2025 draft.
- The draft's 'We repeat this Ansatz - magneto-chiral-boson/fermion partners:' (p. 23) echoes 2012's 'An Ansatz - magneto-chiral-SUSY:' (p. 1).
- The draft does not cite the 2012 paper.

v-winn's evidence '0 occurrences of β' is not reliable. pypdf and MuPDF both extract this PDF's equation-editor glyphs as '!' (201 of them in the MuPDF text). The conclusion still holds: the photon passages (§§5, 7, 8, 10, 16, 20) describe no photon classes and no velocity-dependent coupling.

items.source: Item 4. David R Winn, 'A Heuristic Dual to Ordinary Matter Yielding Composite Self-interacting Scalar Dark Matter', draft dated 'August 17, 2025', 40 pp.; Dropbox file 'A_dual_to_ordinary__August_16.pdf', linked from SUSY 2025 slide 1.
items.quotes_found: All 17, found by code in my pypdf text of the file I downloaded through the same public link (same MD5, 0a5361f2…), each on the page given.
items.relation_corrections:
C6 should be related, not 'not relevant'. The draft proposes Bose condensates of right-handed sneutrinos as dark matter:
- 'may form Bose condensates —hence Dark Matter —in the cosmos.' (p. 26)
- 'These handed complex scalars may form Bose condensates as a part of Dark Matter.' (p. 29)
- 'condensates also contribute to Dark Matter, and may provide the bulk of it' (p. 32, item 27)

This is the momentum-mode condensation of App. A item 3's wave case, though never called momentum space or clumping. The evidence v-winn cites (DR15, magnetic stars and galaxies) concerns the composites, not these condensates.

Add C5: related, theme only (my judgment). Item 36 is 'Photinos as Dark Energy', and p. 34 says 'Dark Energy will change with time, becoming weaker.' There is no collapse.

C7 (no label given): not relevant. The draft calls the di-gluino force 'relatively long Yukawa-like range' (p. 8) and 'a long range force' (p. 24), but the range is set by MeV squark masses (about 86 fm, computed), with no velocity gate.

The other labels hold.
items.note:
Confirmed:
- CreationDate 2025-08-17 00:50:49 UTC; ModDate 2025-08-18 16:54:30 −04:00, which is 20:54:30 UTC.
- Dropbox redirected straight to the file with no login. The Wayback Machine has no capture of the link.
- I read the draft in full. The p. 12 Lagrangian has one potential Aμ. 'The photon is not affected directly' (p. 3). There is no momentum-space or phase-space placement and no Born reciprocity.

Corrections:
- 'It cites earlier monopolium-as-dark-matter work (Vento and Traini 2020; Burdyuzha 2018)' is half wrong. Ref. [10], Eur. Phys. J. C 80 (2020) 62 (arXiv:1909.03952), studies 'the effect of the magnetic dipole field created by a pair of monopole-anti-monopole or monopolium on the successive bunches of charged particles in the beam at LHC' (its abstract). That is not dark matter. Neither [10] nor [46] is cited anywhere in the body: pp. 1–37 carry markers for 46 of the 65 references, and these two are not among them.
- The overall's 'the draft rejects solitons' overstates. The draft adopts elementary monopoles: 'one can consider monopoles as elementary particles' (p. 2); 'pointlike bare-charge magnetic monopoles' (p. 12). But it also says 'While Hooft-Polyakov monopoles must exist in Grand Unified Theories (GUTs), magnetic monopoles do not have to be semi-classical quasiparticles or solitons.' (p. 2). And it takes its charge quantum from the soliton argument: 'according to the doubled Dirac reciprocal prescription for soliton monopoles' (p. 1); 'We assume from the topological arguments of t’Hooft [2] and Polyakov [3] above' (p. 38, ref. [18]).
- The conclusion stands: no soliton localized in momentum.

overall:
I could not refute v-winn's finding in substance; it holds, with corrections of detail.

**What I did.** I downloaded every source myself and used none of v-winn's or the critic's files:
- the Indico pages, export JSON and PDFs for Lepton-Photon, SUSY 2025 and Invisibles25;
- the arXiv abstract page, API record and PDF of 1206.4590;
- the Dropbox draft;
- the Wayback captures for APS, Aspen and DPF.

I extracted the text with pypdf, rendered pages with MuPDF, read all of it, and checked by code.
- All 72 quotations are found again in my own text, on the page or slide given.
- My files are byte-identical to v-winn's: same MD5s, and the Wayback SHA-1 digests equal those of my files.
- The dates hold, including 18 Jun 2012 for arXiv:1206.4590 (v1 only), and the day counts (371, 291 and 5187 full days).
- The core content claims hold. Winn gives one magnetic partner per charged Standard Model particle, under our own photon. The poles are elementary and point-like, and they are hidden by binding into neutral composites. The model is heuristic, with no Lagrangian. Nothing in any version is placed in momentum or phase space, and there is no Born reciprocity.
- The strongest label, C4 shared-photon 'partial', is not stronger than its evidence. Winn has the mirror family and §11.4's binding route but not the p-polarization, and v-winn says so.

**Corrections.**
1. C6 should be related, not 'not relevant' or unlabelled, for the 2012 paper and the draft. Both propose Bose condensates of right-handed sneutrinos as dark matter, which 'may provide the bulk of it'. The Lepton-Photon, SUSY, APS and DPF texts have no condensates.
2. Two first-public dates are earlier; prior art is unchanged. The 2025 abstract was public by 9 Aug 2025 (SUSY timetable capture). The Aspen title was public by 16 Feb 2025, then listed under the presenter Sokratis Trifinopoulos.
3. The draft's ref. [10], Vento and Traini 2020, concerns monopole-pair fields acting on LHC beam bunches, not dark matter. Neither [10] nor [46] is cited in the draft's body.
4. 'The draft rejects solitons' overstates. The draft adopts elementary monopoles but keeps 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles in GUTs and takes its charge quantum from the soliton argument. The conclusion (no soliton localized in momentum) stands.
5. The SUSY deck matches 17 of its 24 slides to Lepton-Photon slides, including the extra slides 26–27, not 'slides 1–23'.
6. The C7 label stands, but Winn does call his di-gluino force long-range (summary p. 3; draft pp. 8, 24). The ranges are microscopic (about 86 fm to 2 nm, computed), and nothing is gated by velocity.
7. The critic has a second error that v-winn did not flag: 'Neither file contains … reciproc' is wrong, since summary p. 1 reads 'reciprocal relationship of electric<=>magnetic charges'.

**Minor.**
- For DPF, '40 days' is a calendar-date difference; the other items count full days.
- The Lepton-Photon upload came 3 min 20.1 s before the talk, not 3 min 21 s.
- The Book of Abstracts shows a missing-glyph box where α and β were, not nothing.
- 'A second published account of the monopole null result … beside Khademi 2009' is loose. The standard account, inflation after a unification transition (flag 59), comes first.
- C5 could read 'related (theme only)' for Winn's photino dark energy (my judgment).

**Searches.** I found no new Winn version in INSPIRE, the arXiv API, the CERN Indico search, five web searches or the Fairfield physics faculty page. The APS 2026 entry 'apr-p92/8' remains unresolved. The other monopole-dark-sector papers my searches met (Vento 2025; Terning–Verhaaren, which the draft lists without citing; Kühne 2025) are already in the record's literature-check files.

**Refusals.** Fermilab Indico answered with a Cloudflare check (HTTP 403), and preprints.org refused the fetch (HTTP 403). I got around neither. The Internet Archive was offline for part of the run, and I retried those queries.

My files are in /home/paul/git/reinholdtsen/conjugate-matter/work/dual-sector/scratch/v-winn-refute/: downloads in dl/, extracted text in txt/, the quotation checker scripts/qcheck.py, and its results in quotes/qcheck_result.json.
